# Approximation Methods - 1

In this chapter we shall consider the time-independent perturbation theory.
That is, the Hamiltonian of the system is written as 
$$
H = H_0 + \lambda H^\op,
$$ {#eq-app1}
where $H_0$ is a Hamiltonian simple enough to be solved exactly and $H^\op$
is a perturbation to it. The parameter $\lambda$ varies from $0$ to $1$ and
determines the "strength" of the perturbation.

Since the system with $\lambda = 0$ is solvable exactly, we know the eigenvalues
and eigenstates of
$$
H_0\ket{n^0} = E_n^0\ket{n^0}.
$$ {#eq-app2}
Our aim is solve
$$
H\ket{n} = E_n\ket{n},
$$ {#eq-app3}
using the solution of @eq-app2. The portion $\lambda H^\op$ is a perturbation,
that is, its impact on the system is small as compared to that of $H_0$. We,
therefore, expect that the eigenvalues and eigenstates of $H$ will not be 
drastically different from those of $H_0$. The procedure to build them depends
on whether the spectrum of $H_0$ is degenerate or not. We will first consider
the simpler case of the non-degenerate spectrum.

## Non-degenerate spectrum
We assume that we can express $\ket{n}$ and $E_n$ as power series of the form
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
E_n &=& E_n^0 + \lambda E_n^1 + \lambda^2 E_n^2 + \cdots \\
\ket{n} &=& \ket{n^0} + \lambda\ket{n^1} + \lambda^2\ket{n^2} + \cdots
\end{eqnarray}
$$
Substituting these forms in @eq-app3, taking into account @eq-app1 and
@eq-app3 and equating the powers of $\lambda$ on either sides of the equation
we get 
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
H_0\ket{n^0} &=& E_n^0\ket{n^0} \\
H_0\ket{n^1} + H^\op\ket{n^0} &=& E_n^0\ket{n^1} + E_n^1\ket{n^0} \\
H_0\ket{n^2} + H^\op\ket{n^1} &=& E_n^2\ket{n^0} + E_n^1\ket{n^1} + 
E_n^0\ket{n^2} \\
H_0\ket{n^3} + H^\op\ket{n^2} &=& E_n^3\ket{n^0} + E_n^2\ket{n^1} + 
E_n^1\ket{n^2} + E_n^0\ket{n^3} \\
\vdots &=& \vdots
\end{eqnarray}
$$
Since $H_0$ is hermitian, multiplying the second of the above equation by 
$\bra{n^0}$ gives,
$$
E_n^1 = \braket{n^0|H^\op|n^0}.
$$ {#eq-app5}
This is the first order correction to the energy eigenvalue $E_n^0$. Likewise,
the second order correction is
$$
E_n^2 = \braket{n^0|H^\op - E_n^1|n^1}
$$ {#eq-app6}
and the third order correction is
$$
E_n^3 = \braket{n^0|H^\op - E_n^1|n^2} - E_n^2\braket{n^0|n^1}.
$$ {#eq-app7}
